ntlpanel: Nighttime Lights to Analysis-Ready Panels for Econometrics

Source: R/ntlpanel-package.R
ntlpanel-package.Rd

ntlpanel turns nighttime lights rasters into balanced unit-by-period panels whose every row says how much of the unit was actually observed.

Details

The workflow has five steps:

  1. Find or fetch data. ntl_sources() lists supported products. ntl_fetch() downloads NASA Black Marble tiles (Suomi NPP VNP46A3/A4 and NOAA-20 VJ146A3/A4) into a cache. ntl_files() indexes files you already have (EOG VNL composites, harmonized DMSP-VIIRS series, Black Marble .h5 files). Both return a manifest.

  2. Extract. ntl_extract() reads one period at a time, applies quality, coverage and gas-flare masks (ntl_mask()) and computes zonal statistics with coverage diagnostics (ntl_aggregate()).

  3. Splice sensors. ntl_splice() puts Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 (or any two series) on one scale and reports level shifts per unit.

  4. Build the panel. ntl_panel() balances the unit x period grid and adds transforms and time indices. ntl_gapfill() applies explicit rules to missing or low-coverage cells, such as the summer stray-light gaps at high latitudes.

  5. Add design variables. ntl_exposure() assigns distance rings and first-treatment dates. ntl_crosswalk() and ntl_apply_crosswalk() move tabular data between boundary vintages.
